body: There's no need to check if `k->is_pressed()`, the above condition should handle it.
I don't think the flag to dismiss it is needed? you should be able to use `symbol_tooltip_timer->stop();`
This one shouldn't be needed, its already set above.

`last_symbol_tooltip_word` can be assigned above, just before `symbol_tooltip_word` is assigned. This way it can be a local variable.

Also it could be based on the `symbol_tooltip_pos` instead of the word, so you can move the mouse on the same symbol after typing to retrigger it.
Where? I don't see it
Some users may not want the tooltip to return if they are still on the word. Having to move off and then back on the word to retrigger tooltips is pretty standard UX
This would only work until the mouse is moved again. The idea is to not show the same tooltip after it has been dismissed.

It feels inconsistent that moving the mouse on the same symbol does re-trigger it unless it was dismissed with a keypress.
Also no other tooltips in the editor require moving off the word and back on to re-trigger, like the inspector.
On the other line it is assigned 769 `symbol_tooltip_dismissed = true;`

> It feels inconsistent that moving the mouse on the same symbol does re-trigger it unless it was dismissed with a keypress.

Well, the reason mouse motion is ignored is because you can accidentally move the mouse while reading the tooltip, having it stay disabled will then be bad UX. There might be a way to not dismiss the tooltip when the mouse is moved unless it moves off the symbol, but that is not within the scope of this PR.

>Also no other tooltips in the editor require moving off the word and back on to re-trigger, like the inspector.

That's true, but that behaviour should not impede this PR, that just means some work must also be done on inspector tooltips, but that is also out of scope for this PR.
There is an issue about inspector tooltips  not being dismissed, but I can't find it at the moment
@kitbdev this is to remove any active tooltip when the code completion rect pops up.

> There might be a way to not dismiss the tooltip when the mouse is moved unless it moves off the symbol, but that is not within the scope of this PR.

If this is addressed in the future then it would probably affect this code, we shouldn't add half of the feature here when it only works in some cases.

Also it is incorrect to use the word to know when to dismiss the symbol because the symbol can be in different contexts that make the tooltip different.
For example if the same word is in a comment or a string, or a variable at the end of a function vs a parameter of another one next to it.
```gdscript
# _enter_tree
func _enter_tree() -> void:
	var myvar1 := "test"
func test1(myvar1 := false):
	pass
```

This is not where code completion pops up though?
Setting it here does nothing because it is always set before this.

> >There might be a way to not dismiss the tooltip when the mouse is moved unless it moves off the symbol, but that is not within the scope of this PR.
>
> If this is addressed in the future then it would probably affect this code, we shouldn't add half of the feature here when it only works in some cases.

I failed to mention the tooltip being dismissed when the mouse is moved is the original behaviour of the system. The way it currently operates is that any key press or mouse motion dismisses the tooltip, the original behaviour is that the tooltip reappears after the timer in such cases (which is set to 1/2 second by default). 

The purpose of this PR is to target that second part and keep the tooltip dismissed if a key is pressed (excluding modifier keys) and to not have the tooltip appear if behind a code completion popup.

I don't know where the behaviour of the tooltip being dismissed when the mouse is moved or a key is pressed happens within the system for the original behaviour, so I can't modify said behaviour to keep the tooltip drawn until the symbol no longer matches.

Most of the logic is in `EditorHelpBitTooltip`, in `editor_help.cpp`, but its kind of hacky compared to regular tooltips.

I think changing it should be in a separate PR.
Yeah, I can work on that in the future as I'm a bit busy right now (working on a feature implementation). It'd be nice if this could get approved as it does what it set out to do.

Currently it still prevents the popup from retriggering after hiding if the word is the same, which as I mentioned above isn't always correct and it half-implements that feature.
So instead of using the word it can use `symbol_tooltip_pos != last_symbol_tooltip_pos` or something instead.
And in that case the `symbol_tooltip_dismissed` shouldn't be needed either like I mentioned in another comment. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/121311#discussion_r3642065783
